properties.decision:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION of the standing contradiction between `dec:merge-survivor-provenance` and the two facts that contradict it (`fact:apply-heal-would-have-destroyed-the-wrong-contributor`, `fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status`). AWAITING ANTHONY'S WORD — recorded at `proposed` with him as approver, so the loop reports it as owed rather than letting it read as settled.

DO NOT RE-OPEN THE PROVENANCE RANKING. It is correct and it is not what fails. The failure is entirely in the TIEBREAK beneath it: provenance ranks authored > planned > imported > reconciled > inferred > healed, and in practice both sides of a real collision are hand-authored, so the rank TIES and `a <= b` on the node id decides. Twice observed, twice choosing the worse node — `req:backend_as_product` (medium, accepted) over `req:graph_is_the_content_bible` (critical, proposed) at dev_storyflow 2026-08-08, and `ctr:anthony` (8 edges, no description) over `who:ajs` (161 edges, full description) here on 2026-08-09.

THE ARGUMENT THAT UNBLOCKS THIS, and it is the whole point of the node: DEGREE IS NOT A POLICY. The reason the rule was deliberately left alone is recorded in `fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status`: ranking priority above status, or the reverse, asserts a claim about what matters more in a design, and `dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement` says reflow2 must not default that — it is the user's. THAT REASONING IS SOUND AND IS NOT BEING OVERTURNED. But "destroy fewer edges" is not a claim about what design content matters; it is a property of the MERGE OPERATION. And the thing it would replace — alphabetical id order — is arbitrary by construction. Substituting a non-arbitrary tiebreak for an arbitrary one asserts no policy at all, which is exactly why this can be done while the priority/status question stays the user's.

FOUR PARTS, SMALLEST FIRST.

(1) WHERE PROVENANCE TIES, BREAK BY DEGREE — keep the node whose deletion destroys less of the design. Degree is already computed and 161 against 8 is not close.

(2) WHERE DEGREE ALSO TIES, REFUSE RATHER THAN PICK. A merge that genuinely cannot distinguish should ask. `dec:ask-not-repair` already holds this shape for the suspicion half; this extends it to the survivor half. A refusal that names both candidates is strictly more useful than a coin toss that names neither.

(3) KEEP PRIORITY AND STATUS OUT OF THE RULE, PUT THEM IN THE DISCLOSURE. "You are deleting a critical, still-unconfirmed node in favour of a medium, accepted one" is INFORMATION, not a policy, and the machinery to say it already exists — `chg:a-merge-proposal-discloses-what-it-would-destroy` built `would_destroy` and the alphabet-chose-the-victim line in August. This adds a sentence to an existing disclosure rather than a rule to an existing ranking.

(4) THE SCORING HALF IS SEPARATE AND PROBABLY WORTH MORE. Similarity is prose-only, unweighted by shared referents, which is what let two requirements sharing no requirement, surface or actor score 81-85. Fixing the survivor rule makes a bad merge less destructive; fixing scoring stops the pair reaching a merge at all. Recorded here so the two halves are not confused, NOT claimed by this decision.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated because the defect count will not move and somebody will look for it: recording this does not clear `heal:0fc0362a90ff913b` or `heal:7456a4d260ca45ce`. The contradiction detector fires on every CONTRADICTS edge whose alignment is not `supporting` and NEVER LOOKS FOR A RESOLVING DECISION, despite its own doc comment and its `suggested_fix_type: generate_decision` saying otherwise. The honest closure path is that when the tiebreak actually changes, the two facts become historical observations about the OLD rule and their CONTRADICTS edges should be retired as part of that change — not silenced now.

EVIDENCE GAP, stated rather than papered over: degree is KNOWN to decide the contributor case correctly (161 v 8). Whether it separates dev_storyflow's pair is UNVERIFIED — that is their graph and it was not read. If their two nodes have similar degree, part (1) helps less than this decision implies and part (4) carries more of the weight.
properties.name: PROPOSED — when provenance ties, the merge survivor is the node whose deletion destroys less, and a genuine tie refuses instead of picking
properties.rationale:
Written at Anthony's request on 2026-08-10 after he asked for the merge-survivor pair in plain English and then for the recommendation to be recorded. The recommendation is mine; the decision is his to make, which is why this is `proposed` with an approver edge rather than accepted.

The load-bearing move is separating the tiebreak from the ranking. Reading `fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status` first is what made that possible — it states plainly that the rule was NOT re-opened on purpose, and names the principle. Without that, the obvious proposal is "consult priority and status", which walks straight into the judgement reflow2 refuses to default and would have been rejected for a good reason. The finding that the blocked path and the open path are different paths came from reading why it was blocked.

Deliberately does not claim the scoring half, and deliberately records the unverified half of its own evidence.
